title: Ensuring Effective and Efficient Agency Logging and Network Visibility to Defend Against Evolving Cyber Threats
summary: Replaces M-21-31 with an adaptive federal logging and network visibility framework centered on continuous event monitoring and investigation, response, and forensics.
executiveHighlights: Prioritizes Continuous Event Monitoring and threat hunting, investigation, response, and forensics.
requirements: Prioritize logs and infrastructure supporting continuous event monitoring.
Maintain logging capabilities supporting threat hunting, investigation, response, and forensics.
applicability: Federal executive departments and agencies addressed by the memorandum.
extractedText: Effective immediately, OMB Memorandum M-21-31 is rescinded. Agencies must prioritize Continuous Event Monitoring and Threat Hunting, Investigation, Response, and Forensics.

changeHistory.description: Seeded and verified against the official OMB PDF.

title: Sustaining Select Efforts to Strengthen the Nation's Cybersecurity and Amending Executive Order 13694 and Executive Order 14144
summary: Amends Executive Orders 13694 and 14144 and sustains selected federal cybersecurity measures, including secure software, routing security, encryption, and post-quantum cryptography actions.
executiveHighlights: Amends rather than wholly rescinds Executive Order 14144.
requirements: Carries forward amended federal actions concerning secure software and cryptographic transition.
applicability: Federal departments and agencies identified in the order.
extractedText: Executive Order 14306 amends Executive Order 14144 and sustains select efforts concerning software security, routing security, encryption, and post-quantum cryptography.

title: Implementing Secure Practices for Cloud Services
summary: Directs federal civilian agencies to implement secure configuration practices for specified cloud services using CISA's Secure Cloud Business Applications baselines.
executiveHighlights: Establishes compulsory cloud security actions for covered FCEB agencies.
requirements: Implement required secure cloud configuration baselines and provide required status information to CISA.
applicability: Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies; exclusions follow the statutory BOD scope.
extractedText: Binding Operational Directive 25-01 requires Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies to implement secure practices for cloud services.

title: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
summary: Provides voluntary guidance for organizations of any size or sector to understand, assess, prioritize, and communicate cybersecurity risk.
executiveHighlights: Adds the Govern function and expands the framework's applicability.
applicability: Organizations of any size, sector, or maturity; use is not universally mandatory.
extractedText: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 provides guidance to industry, government agencies, and other organizations to manage cybersecurity risks.

title: Zero Trust Maturity Model Version 2.0
summary: Provides a maturity model agencies can use to plan and assess progress across five Zero Trust pillars and cross-cutting capabilities.
executiveHighlights: Defines traditional, initial, advanced, and optimal maturity stages.
Supports implementation of the federal Zero Trust strategy.
applicability: Federal agencies implementing Zero Trust; the maturity model itself is guidance.
extractedText: Zero Trust Maturity Model Version 2.0. The maturity model supports agencies in the development of zero trust strategies and implementation plans.

changeHistory.description: Seeded and excerpt checked against the official CISA PDF.

title: Improving Asset Visibility and Vulnerability Detection on Federal Networks
summary: Requires covered agencies to improve asset discovery and vulnerability enumeration capabilities and related reporting to CISA.
executiveHighlights: Establishes measurable asset discovery and vulnerability enumeration performance requirements.
requirements: Perform automated asset discovery at least every seven days.
Initiate on-demand discovery within 72 hours of a CISA request and provide available results within seven days.

deadlines.label: Recurring and request-based deadlines apply; verify current implementation guidance.

applicability: Federal Civilian Executive Branch systems; statutory exclusions apply.
extractedText: The directive focuses on asset discovery and vulnerability enumeration. Agencies must initiate on-demand asset discovery within 72 hours of a CISA request and provide available results within 7 days.

title: Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1: Recommendations for Mitigating the Risk of Software Vulnerabilities
summary: Recommends a core set of high-level secure software development practices that can be integrated into software development life cycles.
executiveHighlights: Organizes practices around preparing, protecting software, producing well-secured software, and responding to vulnerabilities.
applicability: Software producers, purchasers, and consumers; becomes required where incorporated by policy or contract.
extractedText: This document recommends the Secure Software Development Framework, a core set of high-level secure software development practices that can be integrated into each software development life cycle implementation.

changeHistory.description: Seeded from the official NIST CSRC publication page.

title: Moving the U.S. Government Toward Zero Trust Cybersecurity Principles
summary: Sets a federal Zero Trust strategy and requires agencies to meet specified identity, device, network, application, and data goals.
executiveHighlights: Requires specific Zero Trust security goals by the end of FY 2024.
Emphasizes phishing-resistant MFA, device inventory, encrypted traffic, application testing, and data protections.
requirements: Use centralized identity systems and phishing-resistant MFA.
Encrypt DNS requests and HTTP traffic in agency environments.
Maintain complete device inventory and improve detection and response.

deadlines.label: Target date for the memorandum's specific Zero Trust security goals.

applicability: Federal civilian executive branch agencies, subject to the memorandum's scope and exceptions.

zeroTrustExcerpts.excerpt: This memorandum requires agencies to achieve specific zero trust security goals by the end of Fiscal Year (FY) 2024.

extractedText: This memorandum requires agencies to achieve specific zero trust security goals by the end of Fiscal Year (FY) 2024. The goals use five pillars: Identity, Devices, Networks, Applications and Workloads, and Data.

changeHistory.description: Seeded and quoted excerpt checked against the official OMB PDF.

title: Improving the Federal Government's Investigative and Remediation Capabilities Related to Cybersecurity Incidents
summary: Established federal event logging maturity requirements; rescinded effective immediately by M-26-14 in May 2026.
executiveHighlights: Historically established tiered logging maturity requirements.
No longer current policy; consult M-26-14.
applicability: Historical requirements for federal agencies; no longer current after rescission.
extractedText: M-21-31 established event logging maturity requirements. Effective immediately, OMB Memorandum M-21-31 is rescinded by M-26-14.

changeHistory.description: Marked rescinded based on explicit language in M-26-14.

title: Zero Trust Architecture
summary: Defines Zero Trust Architecture concepts, logical components, deployment models, and enterprise use cases.
executiveHighlights: Moves security focus from network perimeters to resources and explicit authentication and authorization.
applicability: Enterprises considering Zero Trust architecture; this publication is guidance, not a universal mandate.

zeroTrustExcerpts.excerpt: Zero trust (ZT) is the term for an evolving set of cybersecurity paradigms that move defenses from static, network-based perimeters to focus on users, assets, and resources.

extractedText: Zero trust (ZT) is the term for an evolving set of cybersecurity paradigms that move defenses from static, network-based perimeters to focus on users, assets, and resources. This document contains an abstract definition of zero trust architecture.

changeHistory.description: Seeded and quoted excerpt checked against the official NIST CSRC page.

title: Develop and Publish a Vulnerability Disclosure Policy
summary: Requires covered civilian agencies to develop and publish vulnerability disclosure policies for internet-accessible systems and maintain supporting processes.
executiveHighlights: Makes vulnerability disclosure policy publication compulsory for covered agencies.
requirements: Develop and publish a vulnerability disclosure policy.
Maintain processes to receive and act on vulnerability reports.
applicability: Federal executive branch departments and agencies except statutory and listed exclusions.
extractedText: Binding Operational Directive 20-01 requires individual federal civilian executive branch agencies to develop and publish a vulnerability disclosure policy for their internet-accessible systems and services.
